did: I built the phone half of RR22: a Rust Rounds week no longer locks after you send it. Until its deadline you can open any ticket, say one again (the take you sent is kept), answer one you skipped, and send the week again. Home keeps only your latest send, and what home has at the deadline is what counts, for good, as you decided. After the deadline the week reads back what home had then: every ticket with its points and program, your takes playable with the words home heard, and "Not answered." for the rest, and it says plainly if a later send didn't reach home in time. I also placed home's two new stores, the draft and the final, in the assurance ledger ahead of the server change. Codex found three real problems along the way, all fixed before merging, the last being a take that could have been deleted if letting it go home failed.

calls.title: A week you already sent opens on its brief
options: Open on the brief, with the words home heard on each ticket's card
Open on the sent screen, with a way back to the week
Open on the first ticket's card
calls.why: The week stays open after a send, so the brief, which says where each ticket stands and what home has, is the way back in.
calls.undo: Have the bundle machine open a week that resends on its sent screen again.

calls.title: Each send holds the whole week, and Send again waits for a change
options: Every send holds the whole week and needs something changed
A send holds only what changed
calls.why: Home keeps only the latest send, so a send of the changed tickets alone would drop the others from what counts.
calls.undo: Drop the merge of the last send in the week's record, and the unchanged need in the bundle machine.

calls.title: After the deadline the week reads back on one scrolling screen
options: The brief only, each ticket opened from it
calls.why: The issue said what the read-back shows, not how it is laid out.
calls.undo: Render the read-back's tickets as read-only cards on the pager.

left: The phone decides by its own clock that a week has closed, so a send made just before the deadline on a phone whose clock runs fast is never sent.
If a send reaches home after the deadline, home refuses it and the phone counts the refusal and tries again until its own clock passes the deadline.
Whether a send counted is read from what the phone last heard home holds, never asked of home, so a phone that didn't hear back can say a send didn't count when home has it.
The next APK must wait until home runs the image with paulgsc/server#770, or the phone keeps retrying its second send of a week.
No clip of the new screens yet: it can be made from the APK once home runs RR22.
